text.text_excerpt: Such a random place to have a fro-yo shop, but this place saved my girlfriend and I on New Years Day when no other fro-yo places were open and we just HAD to have a frozen treat. We were greeted immediately upon walking in by the very nice ladies who worked there. Walking over to the fro-yo section, one is immediately overwhelmed with the amount of different toppings there are. I mean, seriously, I have never been to a fro-yo shop with that many different choices. That being said, the actual fro-yo selection was kind of underwhelming, but we may have just gone in during an off time. It was good, but not Yogurtland good. However, my girlfriend got some crazy yummy concoction of a smoothie,...

I had a late-night sweet craving on our last night in NOLA, so the fiancé and I walked a couple blocks to RPM. I'm not a big sweet eater, but sometimes I need a little something. They have a great (typical) selection of toppings and flavors. The only negative here for me was that if you get your yogurt in a cup it's a $4 minimum, which isn't a big deal, but I didn't want that much. Oh well, I had no problem throwing away what I didn't finish and I totally understand why they do it that way. My favorite thing here? The map on the wall with "Where are you from?" above it. They have little stickers you can place on top of your hometown/state/country on the map. I like stuff like that. Oh and...

How has nobody reviewed this awesome, yet very bizarre yogurt shop yet? I guess people aren't really looking for yogurt in the Bourbon Street area of New Orleans. But after a couple days straight of heavy southern cooking and several po boys and bread puddings, I was dying for something a little lighter for dessert, and this place was exactly what I was looking for. After you get past the strange 50's decor and the Betty Boop memorabilia everywhere, you can see how great this place is.
